newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes shade down after palladium falls.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes shade down after palladium falls.

text.p: The palladium price climbed to a fresh 21-month high on Thursday as worries over supply gripped the market, dealers said.
The concern over palladium stems from major supplier Russia's administrative snarl-up, which has stopped exports since last November. The price has increased by 40 percent since then.
But selling began on a statement from a senior Ministry of Finance official that shipments to Japan, the world's leading importer, could begin next month. Gold reacted more cautiously.
At 1300 GMT, palladium fixed at $155.50 per ounce, after $160.25 earlier, its highest fix since July 28, 1995.
The rare white metal is used in electronic components and is a key element in the catalytic converters which neutralise noxious gases in car exhausts.
Dealers had mixed feelings on the Russian statement and its likely impact on the speculative positions that have been taken against the shortfall and the consequent market tightness.
"The news was ifs and buts, but it was enough for everyone to show their positions and get out. I think there are still quite a few longs in the market," said one dealer.
"Some of them are holding on, waiting to see if there is more news...We could see another $10 (on the downside)."
A bounce could take the price $15 higher, he added.
The drop also helped ease the tightness in the forward market with one-month lease rates quoted at nine percent from 12 percent earlier, he said.
What happened to the other precious metals prices next is also debatable, dealers said. There were no clues from the New York markets which opened in line with Europe.

"The whole complex was held up by the fact that palladium was so strong. There seems to be producer selling in gold and silver doesn't seem to be getting its own way despite physical offtake and it is set to go lower again," another dealer said.
The worst of the squeeze was probably over, he added.
Gold was fixed at $347.60 against $348.05 earlier. The New York Comex May gold futures contract was down $0.30 at $350.10.
"I wouldn't be surprised if it breaks $345.00, certainly by the end of the week. Physical demand seems to be pretty much satisfied at these sort of levels," a dealer said.
"The strength of the dollar and interest rates are encouraging producer sales," he added.
Silver was barely changed at $4.77/$4.79 and platinum was $1.30 firmer at $368.30/$369.30.
